newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks rise at open as golds bounce.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks rise at open as golds bounce.

text.p: * Toronto stocks rose at the open on Tuesday as the battered gold sector bounced back on rising bullion. * Trade was mixed, with declines outpacing advances 220 to 208.
Toronto stocks rose at the open on Tuesday as the recently battered gold sector bounced back on stronger Comex gold prices, but traders said the rebound may be short-lived.

"I guess the concern is whether it's a dead-cat bounce or whether there's more to it...the old dead cat, she don't bounce too high -- (investors may) use the opportunity to sell stocks into (the bounce)," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 11.49 points to 6540.61 in turnover of 7.9 million shares worth C$115 million.
Overall trading was mixed as declines outpaced advances 220 to 208, with 230 issues flat.
The price of Comex August gold rose US$2.90 to US$321.90 on Tuesday after sinking to new 12-year lows on Monday.
The gold sector led nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes higher, gaining 61.37 points or 0.82 percent to 7591.26.
Real estate sank for the second straight day, shedding 26.59 points or 1.13 percent to 2320.87.
* Higher prices helped Canada's major gold miners, including Barrick Gold Corp, whose shares rose 0.95 to 28.75 in healthy trade, and Placer Dome Inc, which gained 0.25 to 19.50.
